title: Fabry–Pérot transmission, d = 5 mm, R = 0.95
caption: The transmission has sharp peaks at every resonance, spaced by the free spectral range c/2nd = 30 GHz. Mirrors of R = 0.95 give finesse π√R/(1 − R) ≈ 61, so each peak is only FSR/F ≈ 0.49 GHz wide: the pattern resolves frequencies about 60 times finer than the peak spacing.
alt: Graph of transmission against frequency offset from -15 to 45 gigahertz: very narrow peaks of height 1 every 30 GHz, each about 0.49 GHz wide.
description: The horizontal axis is frequency in gigahertz (measured from one resonance); the vertical axis is the transmitted fraction.
Peaks of full transmission occur every FSR = 3 × 10⁸/(2 × 0.005) = 30 GHz.
With R = 0.95 the finesse is π√0.95/0.05 ≈ 61, so each peak has full width at half maximum FSR/F ≈ 0.49 GHz.
Between peaks almost nothing is transmitted.
